newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker rates steady, mainly quiet.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker rates steady, mainly quiet.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were generally little changed on Thursday, with very large crude carriers still fairly firm on good enquiry, brokers said.
The 290,000 tonne Golar Stirling was said done at W63 on a Mideast/U.S. Gulf voyage for Vela, while the 260,000 tonne Crown Unity was fixed to Japan at W77.5 for Tonen.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were also steady at W67.5, with Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne vessels) at W82.5.

The Suezmax market in the Mediterranean was dormant, and Aframaxes (80,000 tonners) in both the Med and the North Sea were not much livelier, with rates at W105 and W95/100 respectively, brokers said.
Cross-Med 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged up to W190 on slightly greater enquiry, while in the north they were steady at W205/210.
In the western hemisphere, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes were steady at W122.5 while 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems dipped to W172.5 from W180, brokers said.
